item.aggregated_output:
## Why

Agents need a repeatable way to turn a topic into a browser-based explanation built around one evolving diagram. Separate slides make it harder to preserve the relationships between elements as an explanation develops. A shared scene system can keep those relationships visible while elements appear, move, connect, and change labels, with a caption explaining each step.

This repository currently contains only a README and OpenSpec scaffolding. Establishing an agent skill together with reusable scene components, a working example, and verification tooling gives authors a practical starting point and viewers a consistent experience across screen sizes.

The recommendation is **go with caveats**. Conventional slide tools reduce implementation and maintenance work, but would require adapting the continuous-diagram experience. Shared components are preferable to bespoke presentation code because navigation, layout, and validation can be reused. The ongoing cost is maintaining the renderer and scaffold; initial project compatibility will be bounded, and automated checks will complement human judgment of visual clarity and explanatory quality.

## What Changes

- Add an agent skill that develops a topic into a captioned sequence of states of one evolving diagram and generates a working browser presentation.
- Provide reusable scene components and a player that preserve element identity while supporting appearance, movement, connections, and relabeling.
- Support forward/back navigation, keyboard controls, a focused presenting mode, and a browsing mode with direct step selection.
- Support responsive layouts, readable captions, and reduced-motion preferences.
- Reuse compatible components in an existing project; when they are absent or the host project is incompatible, create a dedicated presentation project without replacing host configuration.
- Use the skill to author a sample presentation explaining how to use the skill itself.
- Provide a reusable automated verification command and require the skill to check generated production builds and browser rendering, address failures, and report unresolved limitations.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `presentation-authoring`: An agent workflow that turns a topic into a presentation, reuses or bootstraps scene components, and verifies its generated output.
- `presentation-scenes`: Reusable diagram elements and captioned step states that preserve identity and support evolving relationships.
- `presentation-viewing`: Responsive presentation and browsing modes, step navigation, keyboard controls, and reduced-motion support.
- `presentation-verification`: Automated production-build and browser checks with reports and screenshots for presentations using the shared system.
- `presentation-example`: A working presentation explaining the skill, produced by exercising its authoring and verification workflow.

### Modified Capabilities

None. The repository has no existing capability specifications or implementation to modify.

## Technical Approach

Use React and TypeScript for reusable components and presentation state, SVG for diagram rendering, and Vite for a static browser build. Model a presentation as a sequence of captioned scene states with stable element identities. Shared rendering and navigation should support both sequential playback and direct step selection, including backward movement, without depending on the viewer having visited earlier steps.

Bundle the skill with reusable components, scaffold resources, and verification tooling so it can work in projects that have not configured the scene system. Bound initial reuse to compatible React/TypeScript projects; provide a dedicated scaffold for other hosts. The generated presentation should run without a hosted application service.

Use Playwright to exercise the production build at representative desktop, tablet, and phone sizes. Verification should visit every step, exercise navigation and mode switching, detect browser errors and observable layout failures, and produce an actionable report and screenshots. The authoring workflow should include visual inspection: a passing build or browser check alone does not establish readability or explanatory quality. Detailed scene contracts, transition behavior, layout rules, and verification criteria belong in the specifications, design, and test plan.

Feasibility references: [Vite production builds](https://vite.dev/guide/build), [Playwright viewport emulation](https://playwright.dev/docs/emulation), and [Playwright screenshot comparisons](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-snapshots).

## Out of Scope

- A visual presentation editor.
- PowerPoint or PDF export.
- Hosted services or automatic deployment.
- Adapters for arbitrary application frameworks.
- Automatic fact-checking of presentation content.
- Automatic certification of visual or explanatory quality.

## Impact

Add a repository-owned agent skill, shared presentation components and player, scaffold resources, a sample presentation, verification tooling, and usage documentation. Introduce React, TypeScript, Vite, and Playwright dependencies for the relevant authoring, build, and test workflows. Authors will need the documented build tooling and browser-test prerequisites; viewers will use the resulting browser presentation.

The shared scene contract will couple generated presentations to the renderer and verifier, so those resources must evolve together. Responsive diagrams, direct navigation, and reduced-motion behavior are material implementation risks to address in subsequent definition and testing artifacts. No breaking changes are expected because the repository has no existing implementation.
